title: The violinist in the metro
summary: A famous young violinist plays in a metro station for an experiment, and almost nobody stops.
paragraphs: At eight o'clock on a Monday morning, a young woman in jeans and a grey {{hoodie}} stood in a busy metro station and opened a violin case. She put the case on the floor in front of her, with a few coins in it, and began to play. For forty minutes, about a thousand people walked past her on their way to work.

Almost nobody stopped. A few people threw coins without looking. A man checked his watch, slowed down for a few seconds and then hurried on. The only people who really paid attention were children. Again and again, a child stopped and {{stared}}, and a parent pulled them gently by the arm, saying, "Come on, we're late."

What the {{commuters}} didn't know was that the woman was Irene Salas, one of the most {{talented}} young violinists in the country. Two nights earlier, she had played at a concert hall where the cheapest ticket cost sixty euros, and every seat was sold. Her violin was more than two hundred years old. The experiment had been organised by a newspaper. They wanted to answer a simple question: do people recognise beauty when they don't expect it?

When the article was published, many readers felt {{guilty}}. Others were angry. "Of course we didn't stop," one wrote. "We were going to work. It doesn't mean we don't care about music." The newspaper received hundreds of letters, and the argument continued for weeks on radio programmes and social media.

Irene herself was not upset. In an interview, she said that the experience had taught her something. "In a concert hall, people come to listen. In a station, the music has to earn their attention," she said. "And the children always stopped. I think we are born knowing how to listen. We just forget." Since then, once a month, she plays in a different metro station. She doesn't announce it. And now, a few more people stop.

commuters.meaning: people who travel regularly to and from work

talented.meaning: having a natural ability to do something well

guilty.meaning: feeling bad because you did something wrong

hoodie.meaning: a soft jacket or top with a part that covers your head

stared.meaning: looked at something for a long time

questions.question: Who stopped to listen most often?
questions.explanation: The only people who really paid attention were children.

questions.question: Why was the experiment organised?
options: To raise money for a charity
To see if people recognise beauty when they don't expect it
questions.explanation: The newspaper wanted to know if people recognise beauty when they don't expect it.

questions.question: How did some readers react to the article?
options: Some felt guilty and others were angry.
They asked for free concert tickets.
questions.explanation: Many readers felt guilty, and others were angry.

questions.question: What does Irene do now?
options: She refuses to play in stations.
She only plays in concert halls.
She plays in a different metro station once a month without announcing it.
She teaches children in the metro.
questions.explanation: Once a month she plays in a different metro station and doesn't announce it.
